standard_prerequisites.name: Cone of a morphism of dg modules
standard_prerequisites.statement: The cone C(f) of a morphism f : X -> Y is the dg module Y direct sum X[1] with differential given by the block matrix of d_Y and the shifted d_X against f.
standard_prerequisites.use: It gives the differential matrix of C(delta[-1]) that is compared with d_B (source lines 1006-1012).

standard_prerequisites.name: Associated triangle of an admissible short exact sequence
standard_prerequisites.statement: An admissible short exact sequence 0 -> K -> L -> M -> 0 of dg modules determines a morphism delta : M -> K[1] and a triangle (K, L, M, alpha, beta, delta).
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the connecting morphism delta whose shift enters the matrix of d_B (source lines 1003-1006).

standard_prerequisites.name: Splitting of an admissible sequence
standard_prerequisites.statement: An admissible short exact sequence of dg modules splits as graded modules, so the middle term can be written as the direct sum of the outer terms.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof chooses splittings to write L = K direct sum M and to identify alpha and beta with the inclusion and projection (source lines 998-1000).

core_obligations: Choose splittings and normalise the pair: use a choice of splittings to write L = K direct sum M and to identify alpha with the natural inclusion and beta with the natural projection (source lines 998-1000).
Compute the differential of the middle term: show that with respect to this decomposition the differential of B is the block matrix whose entries are d_K, delta, 0 and d_M (source lines 1001-1006).

Identify the cone: observe that the cone of delta[-1] : M[-1] -> K has underlying module K direct sum M and the same block matrix as its differential, and conclude that the two triangles are isomorphic (source lines 1006-1012).

proof_roadmap.step: Choose splittings so that L = K direct sum M and alpha, beta become inclusion and projection.
Write the differential of the middle term as the block matrix with entries d_K, delta, 0, d_M.
Compare with the differential of the cone of delta[-1] and conclude the triangles are isomorphic.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-rotate-triangle at source lines 978-995: for a differential graded algebra A and an admissible short exact sequence 0 -> K -> L -> M -> 0 of dg A-modules with associated triangle (K, L, M, alpha, beta, delta), the triangles (M[-1], K, L, delta[-1], alpha, beta) and (M[-1], K, C(delta[-1]), delta[-1], i, p) are isomorphic. The proof at source lines 997-1013 is a direct comparison of differentials, and it is the identification that makes the rotation axiom work: it chooses splittings so that L is written as K direct sum M and alpha and beta become the natural inclusion and projection, then computes the differential of B (the middle term) as the block matrix with d_K, delta and d_M as its entries, observes that the cone of the shifted connecting morphism has the same underlying module K direct sum M and exactly the same differential matrix, and concludes the isomorphism from the identity of the two differentials. The whole point is that the two constructions produce the same matrix, which the statement does not display. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
